target: soc_fan regulator disable and remove error contract
reviewer: Codex static source and target-kernel review; not independent human approval

kernel_api_contract.regulator_disable: Returns a negative error, but the target core can return before decrementing the handle count when the physical disable fails; it can also return an error after _regulator_handle_consumer_disable has decremented regulator->enable_count (for example, a later load update error). On nonzero ret, the driver therefore cannot infer whether its per-handle enable reference still exists.
kernel_api_contract.supply_propagation: When a later error is returned, the core skips coupled balancing and recursive upstream-supply disable; this can leave upstream resources enabled even after the child handle count changed.
kernel_api_contract.force_disable: regulator_force_disable bypasses normal sharing and may turn off a rail used by other consumers; it is not a safe generic remove fallback.

stock_contract.nb_fan_remove: Stock Ghidra remove only removes the sysfs group; the candidate adds timer cancellation, regulator reference drainage, drvdata cleanup, and global-pointer retirement as a declared hardening deviation.
stock_contract.fan_level_set: Stock calls regulator_disable and logs its result before applying PWM; the later PWM result controls the function return, so a successful PWM apply can mask the regulator error. This is preserved stock behavior and remains a declared deviation where wrappers are used.

target_overlay.scope: one matching compatible was found in the mounted zte-devicetree source tree; this does not prove which overlay was applied on the running device

findings.detail: A negative regulator_disable return is ambiguous about whether the regulator handle enable count was decremented. The candidate wrapper conservatively updates its private ownership counter only on success.

nb_fan_remove stops when disable returns an error or the private counter makes no progress, avoiding an unbounded teardown loop. Since fan_level_set retains stock return behavior, teardown may still encounter a regulator error after its internal call.
The target kernel documents force-disable as overriding other consumers; using it would risk disrupting shared rails. The API exposes no per-consumer count reconciliation after the ambiguous error.

The mounted qwjujube device-tree source contains one soc,fan compatible node. This narrows the global-chip concern for that source tree, but does not prove runtime overlay selection or generic multi-instance safety.

disposition: No source change is justified for this failure contract: neither retrying an ambiguous error nor forcing the regulator off is safe for every target-kernel/provider/sharing path. Retain the declared hardening-deviation status and document the provider-failure residual.
limitations: No runtime regulator fault injection, KCSAN, Android boot, or NX809J hardware test.
The review does not promote the driver to static_verified or claim full functional equivalence.
Runtime overlay selection is not established by the source-tree node count.
